command.short: Ask a System One model a choice or score question and get a typed outcome
command.long:
go-decide asks a System One model, Jev by default or clef with --backend clef: a choice (ask) or an ordered rubric (score).
The outcome is decided, uncertain or escalate, and only a decided outcome is one to act on.
eval measures how well the confidence separates clear decisions from contested ones.
The default thresholds (floor 0.5, confident 0.9, the same for each backend) are placeholders until #6.
Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate, 1 to 4 failures; eval exits 0 with a report.

commands.short: Ask a System One model to choose between options
commands.long:
ask puts a choice question to the --backend model (Jev by default) and prints the outcome as a JSON envelope.
Only a decided outcome has a choice; the other two name a leading option only.
Output schema_version: 5. Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate.
commands.example:
go-decide ask --spec decision.json
  go-decide ask --state "all tests passed" --instructions "Ship it?" --option ship="safe to release" --option hold=wait

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(go-decide completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	go-decide completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/go-decide

#### macOS:

	go-decide completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/go-decide

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
commands.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(go-decide completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	go-decide completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_go-decide"

#### macOS:

	go-decide completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_go-decide

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

commands.short: Measure how well Jev's confidence separates clear decisions from contested ones
commands.long:
eval asks Jev one choice question per decision in a labelled set and reports
accuracy, contested AUC, Brier score and precision and recall per threshold.
It measures; it never approves. Both files are validated before any request.
Output schema_version: 5. Exit code 0 when the report is printed.
commands.example:
go-decide eval --decisions testdata/decisions.json --truth testdata/decisions_truth.json
  go-decide eval --decisions past.json --truth past_truth.json --cache-dir .eval-cache

commands.short: Run this CLI as a live MCP server
commands.long: Expose this CLI's command tree as a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Every visible, runnable command becomes a tool, except the reserved __schema, mcp-server, completion, and help commands and any command excluded with mcp.Exclude; tools/call runs the command in machine mode and returns its payload. Serves over stdio by default, or streamable HTTP (loopback unless --allow-non-loopback is set).
commands.example:
go-decide mcp-server
  go-decide mcp-server --transport=http --addr=127.0.0.1:8080
  go-decide mcp-server --transport=http --addr=0.0.0.0:8080 --allow-non-loopback

commands.short: Ask Jev to rate content against an ordered rubric
commands.long:
score rates the state against ordered levels and prints the outcome as a JSON envelope.
Only a decided outcome has a level; the other two name the nearest level only.
Output schema_version: 5. Exit codes: 0 decided, 10 uncertain, 11 escalate.
commands.example:
go-decide score --spec incident.json
  go-decide score --state "checkout fails for half of users" --level minor="cosmetic" --level major="cannot buy"
